summary: @servicetitan/cp-react-hooks preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temporary directory and then invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js, a ~728KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle with shuffled string-array and _0x-style obfuscation. setup.mjs itself uses obfuscator.io-style variable names and inline method-name lookup objects. Both math_init.js and setup.mjs are present at the tarball root even though package.json declares files: ['dist','src'], so the install-time payload is shipped outside the declared file manifest. A React hooks library has no legitimate need for an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time or for an obfuscated install-time bundle. Fetching Bun is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern used to run install-time code under an interpreter that Node-based scanners do not inspect; the installer's machine executes arbitrary obfuscated logic on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
